2892.title: pdd's docs and skills describe versions, commands and steps that do not match the code
2892.body:
## Problem

`docs/USAGE.md:634` (alpha e91221958) says: "Gemini CLI 0.66.0 uses a verified configuration with tools disabled; other Gemini versions are refused until their safety controls are verified."

pdd does not work that way. It checks the installed Gemini CLI through `gemini --help`, and it accepts any version whose help lists the options that read-only Try needs (`--approval-mode`, `--admin-policy`, `--extensions`, `--allowed-mcp-server-names`, `--output-format`). When one is missing, it says which one: "Gemini Try read-only mode requires <option>; update Gemini CLI." (`src/agent-adapters.mjs:94-97`).

So a person who reads the guide thinks they must install exactly 0.66.0, and a person with another version thinks pdd will refuse it.

## Wanted

- The guide describes what pdd does now: Gemini CLI works with any version that has the needed options, and pdd names the option that is missing. It describes only the current state (no "used to" or "no longer").
- No other text in `docs/`, `skills/`, the RUNBOOK or the README names one required Gemini CLI version.

Follows #2872.



## More texts that do not match pdd (docs audit)

A full audit of `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/` and `skills/` found more texts that do not match the code. Fix them in the same PR. Line numbers are on `alpha` after #2889 (package 0.1.15).

### Agents: Gemini CLI is a workflow agent, and the docs often leave it out

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `README.md:20` | "You also need an agent that can use skills" | `pdd setup` and `pdd workflow run` stop unless Codex, Claude Code or Gemini CLI is installed and signed in (`src/workflow-setup.mjs:12-14`, `src/workflow-agents.mjs:4`, `:29`, `src/pdd-cli.mjs:97-101`). |
| 2 | `docs/USAGE.md:6` | "PDD starts Codex with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` and Claude Code with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`." | Gemini CLI also runs with full access, with `--yolo` (`src/workflow-chat.mjs:111`). |
| 3 | `docs/USAGE.md:50`, `:552`; table `:41-48` | "Codex is the default agent." / "Codex is the default agent. Claude Code works too." The table lists only Codex and Claude Code. | Without `--agent`, pdd uses the first agent that is installed and signed in: Codex, then Claude Code, then Gemini CLI (`src/workflow-agents.mjs:4`, `:23-25`). |
| 4 | `docs/cli.md:46` | "Codex is the default agent." | Same as row 3. |
| 5 | `docs/USAGE.md:226` | "Add `--agent claude` to use Claude Code for the whole run." | `--agent gemini` is valid too (`src/command-catalog.mjs:28`). |
| 6 | `docs/cli.md:26` | "uses the `CODEX_HOME` (Codex) or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (Claude Code) of this terminal" | Gemini uses `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`, with the same missing-folder refusal (`src/workflow-chat.mjs:23`, `src/workflow-runner.mjs:399-401`). |
| 7 | `docs/USAGE.md:566` | "says that `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` does not exist" | Same as row 6. |
| 8 | `docs/USAGE.md:355` | "resumes the chat ... (`codex resume` or `claude --resume`)" | A Gemini run resumes with `gemini --yolo --resume ID` (`src/workflow-chat.mjs:111`). |
| 9 | `docs/USAGE.md:559` | "pdd says that `codex` or `claude` is not on PATH" | pdd says "Codex is not installed. Install: URL", "... is not signed in. Run: ..." or "Install Codex, Claude Code or Gemini CLI first." (`src/workflow-agents.mjs:16-17`, `:29`). "not on PATH" is only for herdr, gh and git (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:125-126`). |
| 10 | `docs/USAGE.md:548` | "If your agent is not signed in, the chat stops at a sign-in screen." | `pdd workflow run` checks the sign-in before the run starts, and refuses or uses another ready agent (`src/workflow-agents.mjs:17`, `:23-25`, `:33-42`). |

### Skills and workflows: pdd has six skills and four bundled workflows

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | `README.md:184` | "NAME is `feature`, `bug` or `small-change`." | `BUNDLED_WORKFLOW_NAMES = ['feature', 'bug', 'small-change', 'product']` (`src/command-catalog.mjs:6`). Your own workflow name also works (`src/argument-parser.mjs:71`). |
| 12 | `docs/USAGE.md:226` | "NAME is `small-change`, `bug`, `feature` or the name of your own workflow" | Same as row 11: `product` is missing. |
| 13 | `docs/USAGE.md:251`; `docs/workflows.md:5`, `:7-11`, `:15-19` | "The areas of the three workflows" / "## The three workflows" | Four bundled workflows. `skills/pdd-product/workflow.json`: area `map` [understand, map], gate approve; area `plan` [parts, contracts, plan], gate pr. |
| 14 | `skills/pdd-setup/SKILL.md:21`, `:22` | "Skills: pdd-prompting (the Prompting guide), pdd-feature, pdd-bug, pdd-small-change." / "(NAME: feature, bug or small-change)" | `pdd setup` installs six skills, `pdd-product` too (`src/skills-install.mjs:6`). It copies this block into each repo as it is (`src/project-setup.mjs:8-12`). |
| 15 | `docs/cli.md:13` | "Install the five [PDD skills]" | Six (`src/skills-install.mjs:6`). |
| 16 | `docs/workflows.md:198` | "installs the five PDD skills" | Six. |
| 17 | `docs/USAGE.md:524`, `:531`, `:532` | The uninstall commands name five skills (`pdd-{prompting,setup,feature,bug,small-change}`). Line 533 says "six". | `pdd-product` is the sixth (`src/skills-install.mjs:6`). |
| 18 | `AGENTS.md:10` | "call `pdd-feature`, `pdd-bug`, `pdd-small-change` or `pdd-prompting`" | People also call `pdd-product` (`docs/build-a-whole-product.md:4`, `README.md:57`). |
| 19 | `docs/index.md:5-11` | The docs list has no entry for `docs/build-a-whole-product.md`. | That guide exists. Only `docs/cli.md:204` and the coffee example link to it. |

### Node.js version

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | `README.md:20` | "Node.js 22.20 or newer" | `package.json` `"engines": {"node": ">=22.16.0"}`. `bin/pdd.mjs:6` refuses only `major < 22`. |
| 21 | `docs/cli.md:130`; `docs/USAGE.md:32`, `:39`, `:43` | "Node.js 22 or newer" | Same proof. `CONTRIBUTING.md:7` says 22.16.0. Four files give three different minimums. |

### `pdd setup`

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | `README.md:33` | "`pdd setup` adds a short PDD block ... A second run changes nothing." | Setup first checks for a signed-in agent (`src/workflow-setup.mjs:12-14`). It installs missing skills (`src/pdd-cli.mjs:147-153`) and writes the block (`src/project-setup.mjs:17`). Then it shows the MCP config changes and asks one y/N (`src/agent-mcp-setup.mjs:63-75`). The README names only the block. |
| 23 | `docs/cli.md:13` | The setup row does not say that setup needs a signed-in agent. | Without one, setup stops with exit 1 and changes nothing (`src/workflow-setup.mjs:12-14`). |
| 24 | `docs/USAGE.md:173` | "`pdd setup` ... also installs the skills when they are missing. Both do this:" (3 steps) | Setup also checks the agent first and offers MCP registration last (same proof as row 22). |
| 25 | `skills/pdd-setup/SKILL.md:10` | "The `pdd setup` command writes the same block and also installs the skills when they are missing." | Same as row 22. It writes in the current folder (`src/pdd-cli.mjs:157`, `src/project-setup.mjs:17`). |
| 26 | `README.md:230`; `docs/USAGE.md:78`, `:96` | Run `"$(npm prefix -g)/bin/pdd" setup` to diagnose the PATH. Line 96: "No installation is removed or replaced." | Setup prints the PATH report (`src/pdd-cli.mjs:56-59`), but it also writes the PDD block in the current folder, replaces older pdd skill copies (`src/skills-install.mjs:88`) and asks the MCP y/N. `--version` prints the same report on a conflict and changes nothing (`src/path-diagnostic.mjs:35`). |
| 27 | `AGENTS.md:9` | "`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills` when it is set ... replaces an older copy that has the `.pdd-skill.json` marker" | pdd uses `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when it is an absolute path (`src/skills-install.mjs:101`). It also replaces a marked copy whose files differ or whose marker cannot be read (`:30`, `:32`). |
| 28 | `AGENTS.md:9` | "The order is: install the skills, then the `pdd-setup` skill ..., then the pdd command only for runs with PRs ..." | `README.md:22-33` gives another order: the command, then the skills, then `pdd setup`. |
| 29 | `docs/USAGE.md:176` | "It tells the agent to read `RUNBOOK.md` before a runtime check." | The block says: "Before you write prompts or tests, read RUNBOOK.md in the pdd-prompting skill." (`skills/pdd-setup/SKILL.md:23`) |

### The PDD interpreter

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | `README.md:212`, `:214` | "`pdd test` and `pdd simulate` use the hosted PDD interpreter." / "The skills and the other commands run on your computer." | `pdd lint` (without `--local`) and the Try tools of `pdd mcp` also call it (`src/command-catalog.mjs:89`, `src/try-mcp.mjs:3`, `AGENTS.md:37`). |
| 31 | `docs/USAGE.md:27` | "It needs no PDD account. Only `pdd test`, `pdd lint` and `pdd simulate` use a server" | The `pdd mcp` Try tools also use it. The interpreter needs PDD Cloud approval of your GitHub account: "does not have PDD interpreter access yet. Sign up at https://promptdriven.ai/login" (`src/runtime-client.mjs:471`). |
| 32 | `docs/ISSUES.md:3` | "the PDD interpreter (`pdd test` and `pdd simulate`)" | `pdd lint` also (`src/command-catalog.mjs:89`). |
| 33 | `docs/runtime-boundaries.md:7-12` | The offline-work table does not list `pdd lint --local`. | It sends nothing ("0 AI/network calls", `src/command-catalog.mjs:90`; `docs/cli.md:78`). |

### Workflow runs, gates and PRs

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34 | `AGENTS.md:13`; `docs/cli.md:28`; `docs/workflows.md:30` | "`Stories: N of M pass`" / "`Stories: 4 of 5 pass (✗ refunds)`" | The text is `Stories: N of M Stories pass` (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:608`, `:1971`; `test/workflow-runner.test.mjs:867`, `:888`). |
| 35 | `AGENTS.md:14`; `docs/workflows.md:156`; `docs/USAGE.md:334`, `:545` | "pdd does not run tests" / "pdd does not run the tests itself." / "pdd does not run or check the tests." | `pdd workflow prove` runs the given test command on the base and on the head (`src/workflow-prove.mjs:190`, `:231`; `src/command-catalog.mjs:32`). |
| 36 | `README.md:161` | "In a workflow run, pdd opens two pull requests:" | Only `feature` and `bug` open two. `small-change` and `product` open one (their `workflow.json`). |
| 37 | `docs/cli.md:105`; `docs/workflows.md:87`; `docs/USAGE.md:246` | "After the last step of an area with a PR gate, push the branch and open the PR" | For an area with `"before":"approve"` (prompt-pr, PR 1 in feature and bug), the last step opens an approve gate. pdd opens the PR only after approval (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:1185`, `:1194-1200`). |
| 38 | `docs/workflows.md:122`; `docs/USAGE.md:318` | The quoted question ends "To make the code PR later, run `pdd workflow approve N`." | pdd asks: "To make the code PR later, tell your agent, or run pdd workflow approve N in a terminal." (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:299`, `:1089`) |
| 39 | `docs/workflows.md:28`; `docs/USAGE.md:261` | The story-gate chat "ends with 'Reply in your own words here or run `pdd workflow approve N`, or tell me what to change.'" | No such text is in `src/` or `skills/`. The agent writes its own words (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:1214`, `skills/pdd-feature/SKILL.md:25`). |
| 40 | `docs/workflows.md:132` | "PR-top rendering and old-code proof depend on the runner integration (#2594 and #2570)." | The runner does both today (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:24-26`; `src/workflow-pr-evidence.mjs:98-115`; `src/workflow-inventory.mjs:284-300`). #2594 is closed. |
| 41 | `docs/workflows.md:162`, `:167` | "When a check on the PDD interpreter ran, the body starts with its `Prompt tests` lines" / "The PR begins with the validated replay status" | A code PR body starts with `Old-code proof:`, `Tests vs base:` and the agent notes. Then come `✗ N vectors fail` and the replay status, then the Prompt tests lines (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:908`, `:916`). |
| 42 | `docs/workflows.md:96-97` | "pdd preserves the old parent shell workspace, records it as superseded" | No code records a supersession. The test checks that the old shell stays unchanged (`test/workflow-runner.test.mjs:1966-1968`). |
| 43 | `docs/workflows.md:188-196` | "look for a folder `pdd-NAME` ... The first one found wins." (the list includes `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`) | A home copy cannot replace a bundled workflow: "only a project may override a bundled workflow" (`src/workflow-areas.mjs:53-55`). |
| 44 | `docs/workflows.md:227`; `docs/USAGE.md:462` | "`pdd workflow list  # pdd-mybug is in the list`" | The list shows `mybug`, without `pdd-` (`src/workflow-areas.mjs:51`, `:83-84`). |
| 45 | `docs/workflows.md:252-266` | The example `workflow.json` of the copied pdd-bug, and the field list, have no `replay_evidence`. | The copied file has `"replay_evidence":"pdd.replay-evidence.v1"` on the code area (`skills/pdd-bug/workflow.json:4`). It is valid only on a `pr` area (`src/workflow-areas.mjs:33-34`). |
| 46 | `docs/replay-evidence.md:55` | "For not_run, command and exit_code may be null" | `exit_code` must be null; only `command` may be null (`src/workflow-replay.mjs:366`). |
| 47 | `docs/cli.md:48` | "No command has a time limit." | `pdd workflow prove` stops each phase after 120 s (`src/workflow-prove.mjs:231`). `pdd lint` from an agent waits 90 s by default (`src/runtime-client.mjs:33`). |
| 48 | `docs/USAGE.md:212` | "also run `git remote set-head origin -a`, so Git knows the new one." | pdd reads the default branch from GitHub (`gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`, `src/workflow-github.mjs:94-99`). No code reads `origin/HEAD`. |
| 49 | `docs/USAGE.md:570` | "`approve` says that pdd sees an agent environment" | pdd prints no such text. In an agent session without `--said`, it prints how to relay with `--said`. In strict mode it says "Only the person can approve in a terminal. Run pdd workflow approve N in a normal terminal." (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:293-297`, `:1491-1492`) |
| 50 | `docs/USAGE.md:495` | `herdr session delete pdd` | `herdr session --help`: "delete  Delete a stopped session". A running session must be stopped first (`herdr session stop`). |

### `pdd test`, local files and uninstall

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 51 | `docs/USAGE.md:367`, `:539` | "pdd keeps run state in `~/.pdd/runtime`, never in your repo." The leftovers list has no `.pdd/`. | `pdd test` keeps a cache in the repo at `.pdd/cache/test/` and adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (`src/runtime-client.mjs:2283`, `:2310`). `pdd simulate --cli` writes `.pdd/try/` (`src/try-doors.mjs:40`, `:88`). |
| 52 | `docs/USAGE.md:388` | "`pdd test  # check every story; one table and a report link for each`" | By default it reuses unchanged passing Stories from `.pdd/cache/test/` and does not send them (`src/pdd-cli.mjs:179`, `src/runtime-client.mjs:2425`, `src/runtime-output.mjs:239-241`). `--lf` and `--cache-clear` are not shown. |
| 53 | `docs/USAGE.md:527-535` | Uninstall removes "the skills that `pdd setup` copied, and its state" with `rm -rf ~/.local/state/pdd`. | pdd also keeps state in `~/.pdd` (`src/runtime-client.mjs:137`, `src/agent-adapters.mjs:30`). `pdd setup` can add a `pdd` MCP entry to `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.claude.json` and `~/.gemini/settings.json` (`src/agent-mcp-setup.mjs:59-70`). After uninstall, that entry points to a missing file. |
| 54 | `skills/pdd-bug/steps/try.md:3`; `skills/pdd-feature/steps/try.md:3` | "Set that ceiling with `pdd simulate STORY --max-calls N`" | pdd refuses a higher N for a simulation that is already open (exit 5, `src/runtime-client.mjs:2753`). A new one starts at 400 (`:2793`). The skills offer an early simulation (`skills/pdd-bug/SKILL.md:25`, `skills/pdd-feature/SKILL.md:25`). |
| 55 | `docs/USAGE.md:638` | "The agent cannot run a Simulator action or edit the project." | The chat can ask the page to run an action, with `run: true` and a valid fill (`src/agent-chat.mjs:7`, `src/agent-adapters.mjs:162`). Line 613 of the same file says this. |

### Other

| # | Where | The text says | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 56 | `CONTRIBUTING.md:11` | `node --test examples/ticket-status/test/status.test.mjs` | That folder does not exist. `examples/` has only `coffee-pickup` and `fakes`. |
| 57 | `docs/build-a-whole-product.md:60` | "If trusted duplicates exist, pdd uses the oldest issue and warns." | pdd prefers the issue of a local run first, then the oldest (`src/product.mjs:348-349`, `:390-391`). |
| 58 | `docs/build-a-whole-product.md:61` | "Long issue titles use a Story count or range" | A long title gets a count only: `` ` (${run.stories.length} Stories)` `` (`src/product.mjs:555`). |
| 59 | `docs/build-a-whole-product.md:47-48` | The guide does not say which agent `pdd product start` uses without `--agent`. | It uses Codex and checks no sign-in (`src/pdd-cli.mjs:81`, `src/product.mjs:560`). `pdd workflow run` uses the first ready agent. See #2893, row 6. |
| 60 | `skills/pdd-product/references/files.md:25` | "The small path needs no separate plan." | Only a small map with exactly one part gets runs without `product/plan.md` (`src/product.mjs:232`). Else pdd stops: "product/plan.md: no planned runs." (`:233`) |
| 61 | `skills/pdd-bug/steps/review.md:3` = `skills/pdd-feature/steps/review.md:3` | The reviewer reads the "`Tests vs base:` evidence". | pdd writes `Tests vs base:` only when it publishes the code PR, after the review step (`src/workflow-runner.mjs:946`, `:969`, `:1094-1098`). The review cannot see it. |

### Steps that do not ask for lines that pdd reads

| # | Where | The gap | What pdd does (code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 62 | `skills/pdd-bug/steps/reproduce.md` | No bug step asks for `Defect:` and `Not caught because:`. `review.md:3` reads them. | In a bug run, pdd takes these labels only from the reproduce step (`src/workflow-pr-evidence.mjs:83`). `skills/pdd-small-change/steps/scope.md:6` asks for them. |
| 63 | `skills/pdd-bug/steps/verify.md` | No bug step asks for `Proof (defect fixed):`, `Proof (gap closed):` or `Not fixed yet:`. `skills/pdd-bug/SKILL.md:10` requires "Not fixed yet" for warning-light-only work. | pdd takes `Proof (...)` only from verify and `Not fixed yet:` only from build or verify (`src/workflow-pr-evidence.mjs:83`). The code PR says `Refs #N` only with `Not fixed yet:`, else `Closes #N` (`:118`). The feature and small-change verify steps ask for these lines. |
| 64 | `skills/pdd-bug/steps/verify.md`; `skills/pdd-small-change/steps/verify.md:4` | Neither step names `pdd workflow prove`. | Each code PR gets `Old-code proof:`; without a saved proof it says "not run" (`src/workflow-pr-evidence.mjs:105`). Only `pdd workflow prove` saves the proof (`src/workflow-prove.mjs:208`). |

### Limits for the fix

- `test/skills.test.mjs:133` pins the `skills/pdd-setup/SKILL.md:21` sentence word for word. Row 14 changes both.
- Skill size limits (`test/skills.test.mjs:27-28`): SKILL.md 3072 B (bug and feature 4096 B), step file 1228 B (review 2304 B). The bug and feature `review.md` must stay the same, and keep the `Defect:`, `Not caught because:`, `Old-code proof:` and `Tests vs base:` labels (SKILLS36).
- `test/docs-first-time.test.mjs` fails on history words. Describe only the current state.
- Not in scope: `RUNBOOK.md` and `skills/pdd-prompting/` (the Prompting guide owner reviews those separately), and the help texts in #2893 (they need a code change).

3012.title: Give each PDD repository a reusable, proven way to verify its real app
3012.body:
## Planning status
Nov 5 meeting proposal. Serhan asked us to create this issue for discussion before implementation. Do not start an Autopilot worker or change product code for this proposal until its scope is agreed.

## User need
Agents should reproduce a reported problem and verify the fix in the actual CLI, UI or service without a person explaining how to start and drive the app on every issue. Green unit tests alone can miss the user's failure.

## Proposed outcome for discussion
- During setup or explicit verification setup, inspect the repository for its supported start command, usable-ready signal, existing test driver, data/auth requirements, observable outputs, isolation and cleanup.
- Reuse existing harnesses. Save a small repository-local verification recipe with launch, environment/build check, real user action, evidence capture and cleanup. Reference existing PDD Stories and criteria; do not create a competing requirements system.
- Prove the recipe once end to end on a real mapped feature. A fresh agent must be able to follow it. Preserve evidence after cleanup and state any environment differences still untested.
- Bugs require reproduction on the affected surface and a check that the repaired behavior works there. Use executable old/new regression proof where appropriate. Test real side effects as well as final screen/output.
- Independent verification consumes the actual artifact and evidence. Required behavior that was not exercised remains unproved. Use Runtime when applicable and available; native proof must execute the native behavior it claims to prove.
- Update verification instructions when the app changes without weakening a user journey to hide a product regression. A recurrence records the actual failing case and checks the installed build before another proposed fix.
- Pilot in PDD and Pocket, then a fresh small CRM repository. Include restart and isolated parallel execution so this does not depend on Serhan's local setup.

## Discussion needed
Choose the smallest PDD-owned recipe format and its entry point. Reuse current Stories, workflow steps and evidence rather than importing another framework wholesale. Automatic merge policy is a separate decision; no small-change-only rule is proposed here.

## References and related work
https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md
https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md
#2954 and #2961 provide native-proof/coverage support; #2958 concerns comparing old and fixed code; #2964 is the dependency viewer, not real-app verification.

## Additional main-session use case: compile success is not native scenario acceptance

An anonymized mixed Rust/Python native-integration session provides another concrete recipe-design case. This is application verification experience, not a newly demonstrated PDD CLI or Prompt Runtime defect.

The retained sequence separated:
- Successful pinned upstream baseline compilation.
- Successful composed component compilation.
- Actual native scenarios stopping before their intended target because real host configuration refused the requested feature setup.
- Later scenarios reaching the router but failing an application-owned comparison between the actual qualified tool name and a plain-name expectation.
- A later successful native boundary case while the remaining scenario acceptance was still pending.

Several corrections belonged to the application's own source contracts, composition anchors, fixture byte types and bindings. They should not be filed as Prompt Runtime service failures merely because a native harness uses the word runtime.

For the proposed reusable recipe, preserve distinct statuses for source/context availability, composition/dependency resolution, compilation, test collection, readiness, execution of the intended boundary and actual criterion checks. Record which native target was reached and what blocked it; one compiled artifact or one passing case cannot substitute for the complete required scenario inventory.

Tie the recipe to the exact source/artifact and required environment, including typed fixture construction, platform/browser capabilities and deterministic readiness/custody gates. A fresh verifier should be able to follow it without accessing another agent's histories or substituting fabricated host authority.

This extends the planning use cases only. #2954/#2961 already supply native evidence/profile acceptance mechanisms; it does not establish a regression in them or authorize implementation of this planning proposal. No private application source, host identity, live credential, raw receipt or capability URL is attached.

3246.title: Merge lane is too slow for 40 merges a day: one extra tick per merge, and the next PR waits for the next tick
3246.body:
## Problem
The merge lane is too slow for the goal of 40 merges per day. It takes one PR at a time, and it moves only on the 10-minute tick. Each merge also loses one extra tick:
- `enterLane` adds the label `pdd:merge-lane` and then reads the label list at once.
- GitHub's list does not show the new label yet, so the tick returns "wait" (`if (!now.length) return 'wait'`).
- The next tick, 10 minutes later, finds the label and goes on.
When the lane frees, the next green PR waits for the next tick too.

## Evidence
- Chaos test note 4 (Nov 11, 0.1.28): every merge cost one more tick because of the label read lag.
- Sandbox merges came 30 to 50 minutes apart (median 30 minutes). So the lane does at best about one merge per 30 minutes, about 48 per day with no gaps at all.
- The target is 40 merges per day (Nov 13).

## Proposal
- After the lane label write, read the PR's own labels (`GET issues/N`) in the same tick, which is consistent. Do not wait for the list to catch up.
- When the lane frees (a merge, an END or a release of the lane holder), run the next lane step for the next green PR at once, in the same tick.

## Test
- A fake GitHub whose label list is empty right after the write, while the PR's own labels show the lane. Expect the lane step to go on in the same tick.
- Two green PRs in the queue. After the first merges, expect the second to enter the lane in the same tick.
- Core factory timing: two queued green PRs merge in fewer ticks than today.

3249.title: Keep a checklist from the issue, apart from the builder's scope, and show which items the evidence covers
3249.body:
## Problem
The builder decides the scope of its PR. Nothing keeps the full list of what the issue asks for. So a PR can pass every check and still leave items of the issue undone, and it is called complete.

## Evidence (funnel audit, Nov 9 17:00 to Nov 11 17:00 UTC)
- pdd #2892: the first PR (#3165, old engine) left checklist items of the issue pending. A later core PR (#3222) covered the full docs issue.
- pdd #3012: the work lacked the pilot that the issue requires.
- Narrow passing tests did not show the whole outcome.

## Proposal
- At job start, the engine takes a checklist from the issue text: task-list items, "Done when" and "Expected" sections, and acceptance criteria. It keeps this list apart from the builder's scope.
- The PR body lists each item with its evidence (a test, a check or a file), or with an exclusion that the issue supports (a quote).
- The fresh reviewer checks each item. An item with no evidence and no supported exclusion is a must-fix.
- The merge note shows "checklist: N of M covered".

## Test
- A fake issue with 3 checklist items, and a PR that covers 2. Expect a review must-fix that names the third item, and no merge.
- The same PR with a quoted exclusion from the issue for the third item. Expect a pass.
- An issue with no checklist. Expect no checklist line and no new red.

3260.title: Autopilot waits forever when GitHub Actions does not start a run (personal account minutes or spending limit)
3260.body:
## Problem
Autopilot waits forever when GitHub Actions does not start a run. This is common for a person's private repository: GitHub gives a fixed number of free Actions minutes per month, and the spending limit is often $0. Many people will run Autopilot on a repository like that, not in an organization with paid minutes.

## Evidence (Nov 11)
- From about 20:20 UTC, no Actions run started in the private repositories of one personal account (our sandbox and a new-user trial repository). The runs stayed "queued" with no job, and GitHub refused to cancel them. GitHub's status page said Actions worked. Repositories in the organization ran normally.
- The sandbox PR #106 had a review PASS and a green local full suite at its exact head (198/198 at 20:39 UTC). It waited in the merge lane for more than an hour with no CI result. Nothing merged, and nothing told the person why.
- This week the sandbox used many Actions minutes: each repair push starts a new CI run.

## Proposal
1. Detect it. A CI run for the PR head that stays queued with no started job for 20 minutes, or that fails with a GitHub billing or spending-limit message, means "CI did not start".
2. Do not blame the issue. This is a service-owned stop: no strike, no END, no repair.
3. Tell the person once. One line in `pdd autopilot status` and one alert: "GitHub Actions does not start runs in this repository (queued since HH:MM). This is often the account's Actions minutes or spending limit: Settings → Billing → Actions." No repeated alerts.
4. Hold new intake while CI does not start, so agents do not use tokens on work that cannot merge. Resume by itself when a CI run starts again.
5. Merge rule when CI does not start (decision below):
   - A: wait until CI works.
   - B: when the repository has no required status check, merge on the local full suite that Autopilot already runs on the exact head, and write "CI: did not start (reason); local full suite passed at HEAD" in the merge note. When a required check exists, wait (A).
6. Use fewer minutes:
   - the CI workflow that pdd setup writes uses `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`, so a new push cancels the old run;
   - Autopilot opens PRs as drafts and marks them ready only at the final head, with the workflow running on ready PRs only.
7. `pdd autopilot doctor` shows the Actions minutes left when the GitHub token can read billing, and says how to grant that.

## Test
- A fake GitHub whose CI run stays queued: after 20 minutes the job is held with the service reason, one alert, no strike, and new intake stops. When a run starts, intake resumes.
- Rule B with no required check: the PR merges with the CI line in the note. With a required check: it waits.
- The setup workflow has the concurrency group, and a second push cancels the first run.

## Decision
A or B as the default.

Related: #3246 (merge lane), #3181 (red main), #3238 (stop owners), #3242 (new users).
